citations.quote: The Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) and Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF) have formally endorsed the presidential candidacy of Vice President Leni Robredo and the vice-presidential bid of Davao City Mayor Sara Duterte.
The two groups announced their decision to support the two in a joint statement signed by MILF chairman Al Haj Murad Ebrahim and MNLF chairman Muslimin Sema and was released on Saturday, May 7.

"The two organizations have agreed to support the presidential candidate with a clear platform of governance and commitment to the peace process and the full implementation of all signed agreements during and beyond the current transition period,” the statement read. Earlier, the MILF and its political party , the United Bangsamoro Justice Party (UBJP) announced their endorsement of Robredo last April 23, her birthday. The MILF and MNLF, in their letter, also acknowledged the consequence of their endorsement of Robredo and Duterte, who belong to rival political factions. "Both Fronts are aware of the political consequences of this declaration, especially in consideration of the extended transition period for the establishment of the Bangsamoro Government," the groups added.

citations.quote: A graphic is making the rounds on Facebook with the claim that the Moro Islamic Liberation Front and Iglesia ni Cristo have declared their support for Vice President Sara Duterte.
This is fake and artificially generated.

The overlaid text reads: MILF AT INC, NAGDEKLARA NG SUPORTA KAY VP SARA DUTERTE (MILF and INC declare support for VP Sara Duterte) Panawagan ng mga taga suporta SAMA SAMA TAYO SA 2028 (The call of supporters Let us band together in 2028) The graphic, designed like a poster, bears the polished look of an AI-generated image created using prompts.
There are no endorsements or any official announcement from the website of INC or Luwaran of the MILF.
The official FB page of the MILF Chairman and the Office of the Vice President (OVP) are likewise silent.
Media outlets have not reported any official alignments between the vice president and these groups, following a check of the official social media pages of ABC-CBN , GMA , and TV5 .
